server.host.long.text: The IP address or hostname the server will bind to. Use '0.0.0.0' to allow connections from any device on your network, or '127.0.0.1' (localhost) to restrict access to this machine only.

server.port.long.text: The network port number the server will listen on for incoming connections. Ensure this port is not blocked by your firewall and is not already in use by another application.

server.name: Server Name

server.name.long.text: A descriptive name for this server instance, useful for identification in logs and monitoring.

server.processName.long.text: The internal process name used to ensure only a single instance of the server is running at any time.

server.instanceCheck.enabled.long.text: When enabled, the server prevents multiple instances of the application from running simultaneously, avoiding conflicts.

server.instanceCheck.bufferSize.long.text: The size of the memory buffer used for checking running instances. It is recommended to leave this at its default value.

server.max_connections.long.text: The absolute maximum number of simultaneous client connections the server will accept before rejecting new ones.

server.timeout.long.text: The maximum duration in seconds the server will wait for an idle connection before automatically closing it.

database.path.long.text: The absolute or relative path to the SQLite database file where application data will be stored.

database.session.acquireTimeoutMs.long.text: The maximum time in milliseconds the application will wait to acquire a database session before failing.

database.session.acquireBackoffMs.long.text: The time in milliseconds to wait before retrying a failed attempt to acquire a database session.

database.session.poolMin.long.text: The minimum number of database sessions to keep open and ready for use at all times.

database.session.poolMax.long.text: The maximum number of concurrent database sessions allowed to be open simultaneously.

database.vector.enabled.long.text: Enables the sqlite-vec extension to allow highly optimized vector-based search for duplicate image detection.

database.vector.extensionPath.long.text: The file path to the sqlite-vec extension binary (e.g. vec0.dylib or vec0.so). Required if vector search is enabled.

logging.level.long.text: The detail level of application logs. Typical values include 'debug', 'info', 'warn', and 'error'.

logging.level.options: trace, debug, info, warn, error, fatal

logging.enable_console.long.text: When enabled, log messages will be printed directly to the standard output or console.

logging.enable_file.long.text: When enabled, log messages will be written and saved to log files on the disk.

files.manager.enabled.long.text: Enables the internal file manager responsible for scanning and tracking files.

files.manager.scan.intervalMs.long.text: The delay in milliseconds between consecutive file scanning operations.

scheduler.jitter.enabled.long.text: Introduces slight, random variations to task scheduling to prevent simultaneous executions that could spike resource usage.

scheduler.jitter.percent.long.text: The maximum percentage by which scheduled task intervals can vary when jitter is enabled.

scheduler.drift.mode.long.text: Defines how the scheduler handles task execution delays, whether it should catch up or maintain fixed intervals.

scheduler.drift.maxDriftMs.long.text: The maximum allowed drift in milliseconds before the scheduler resets a task's timing.

scheduler.backoff.enabled.long.text: Allows the scheduler to dynamically increase the interval between task executions when failures or idle periods occur.

scheduler.backoff.initialMs.long.text: The starting delay in milliseconds when the scheduler first begins backing off a task.

scheduler.backoff.multiplier.long.text: The factor by which the backoff delay increases with each subsequent failure or retry.

scheduler.backoff.maxMs.long.text: The maximum possible delay in milliseconds the backoff strategy will reach.

scheduler.backoff.jitterPercent.long.text: The maximum percentage of random variation applied to backoff delays to prevent synchronized retries.

tpm.pool.max.long.text: The absolute maximum number of worker threads the Thread Pool Manager (TPM) can spawn.

tpm.killTimeoutMs.long.text: The maximum time in milliseconds to wait for a thread to finish its work before forcing it to stop.

tpm.thread.idleTimeoutSeconds.long.text: The time in seconds an unused thread remains active before it is automatically terminated to save resources.

tpm.types.fileScan.share.long.text: The relative share or proportion of the thread pool allocated specifically for file scanning tasks.

media.processor.enabled.long.text: Enables the component responsible for extracting metadata and processing media files.

media.processor.intervalMs.long.text: The delay in milliseconds between continuous media processing batches.

tpm.types.media_processor.share.long.text: The proportion of the thread pool allocated for general media processing tasks.

tpm.types.image_processor.share.long.text: Reserved proportion of the thread pool for specialized image processing tasks.

tpm.types.audio_processor.share.long.text: Reserved proportion of the thread pool for specialized audio processing tasks.

tpm.types.video_processor.share.long.text: Reserved proportion of the thread pool for specialized video processing tasks.

media.image.timeoutMs.long.text: The maximum time in milliseconds allowed to process a single image before giving up.

media.image.retry.enabled.long.text: Automatically retry processing an image if a temporary error occurs.

media.image.retry.maxAttempts.long.text: The maximum number of times to retry processing an image after the initial attempt fails.

media.image.retry.baseDelayMs.long.text: The starting delay in milliseconds before the first retry attempt for image processing.

media.image.onnx.modelPath.long.text: The file path to the ONNX machine learning model used for extracting image features and embeddings.

media.image.onnx.inputSize.long.text: The required dimensions (width and height) for images fed into the ONNX model.

media.image.onnx.sessionCache.enabled.lo.text: Keeps ONNX inference sessions in memory to significantly speed up processing multiple images.

media.image.onnx.sessionCache.maxSession.text: The maximum number of ONNX sessions to keep cached in memory simultaneously.

media.image.embeddingDim.long.text: The size of the mathematical vector (embedding) generated for each image. Must match the output size of the ONNX model.

debug.enabled.long.text: Activates additional internal checks, metrics, and capabilities used for troubleshooting.

debug.verbose.long.text: Produces highly detailed debug logs, useful for deep technical investigation but may impact performance.

file_monitoring.enabled.long.text: Actively listens for changes in the file system (e.g., new, modified, or deleted files) to keep the database up-to-date.

file_monitoring.interval.long.text: The delay in milliseconds between polling the file system for updates, if continuous monitoring is not available.

validation.enabled.long.text: Performs checks to ensure data integrity and configuration correctness.

validation.strict.long.text: Enforces rigorous validation rules, refusing to start or process data if any minor inconsistencies are found.

duplicates.finder.enabled.long.text: Activates the core duplicate finder engine to analyze and identify similar or identical files.

duplicates.finder.intervalMs.long.text: The delay in milliseconds between automated duplicate detection sweeps.

duplicates.finder.batchSize.long.text: The number of files processed together in a single duplicate detection operation.

duplicates.finder.maxGroupSize.long.text: The absolute maximum number of similar files allowed to be clustered into a single duplicate group.

duplicates.group.joinDeficitRatio.long.text: How many times further from a group's lead image a photo may sit than from its own closest match anywhere in the library, and still be filed in that group. At the default of 2, a photo joins only if the lead image is within twice the distance of its best match.

Without this check, a whole afternoon of similar frames collapses into one group: every frame clears the similarity threshold against the same lead image even though each has a near-identical twin elsewhere. Lower values split groups more aggressively; 0 turns the check off.

search.placesDbPath.long.text: Path to the offline place database (GeoNames-derived SQLite built by scripts/build_places_db.py). When present, every photo with a GPS fix gets place names (town, region, country, park, nearby landmarks) resolved entirely on this machine — nothing is sent to the internet. When absent, place names stay unresolved. Place data © GeoNames, CC BY 4.0.

search.places.landmarkRadiusM.long.text: Named features (waterfalls, peaks, lakes, monuments, campgrounds, trails) within this many metres of a photo's GPS fix are attached to it as landmarks and become searchable by name.

search.places.settingAtM.long.text: How close a photo must be to a feature of the named kind for searches like "waterfront photos" or "on the beach" to match it. "Near the lake" uses the landmark radius instead.

search.places.localityMaxKm.long.text: How far to look for the nearest populated place when naming a photo's location. Photos further than this from any town get no locality (and therefore no region/country) but still get landmarks and park containment.

duplicates.finder.knnK.long.text: The number of nearest neighbors to retrieve during a vector search. A higher value increases accuracy but requires more computation.

tpm.types.duplicate_finder.share.long.text: The proportion of the thread pool allocated for identifying duplicate files.

duplicates.threshold.similarity.long.text: This dual slider controls two key properties that define how images are grouped:
**Similar Threshold (Green/Down)**: Sets the maximum allowed visual distance to cluster images into a group. A higher value casts a wider net, grouping looser similarities together.
**Exact Threshold (Red/Up)**: Sets the strictness for identifying identical matches. A lower value requires a near-perfect match to be considered an exact duplicate.

**In Combination**: The Similar threshold defines the boundaries of the entire group cluster, while the Exact threshold highlights the truly identical pairs within that specific group for operations like auto-eject.

duplicates.threshold.duplicate.long.text: This dual slider controls two key properties that define how images are grouped:
**Similar Threshold (Green/Down)**: Sets the maximum allowed visual distance to cluster images into a group. A higher value casts a wider net, grouping looser similarities together.
**Exact Threshold (Red/Up)**: Sets the strictness for identifying identical matches. A lower value requires a near-perfect match to be considered an exact duplicate.

**In Combination**: The Similar threshold defines the boundaries of the entire group cluster, while the Exact threshold highlights the truly identical pairs within that specific group for operations like auto-eject.

duplicates.purity.order.long.text: A prioritized list of criteria (like resolution, file size, or date) used to automatically determine the 'best' original file in a duplicate group.

cache.thumbnail.location.long.text: The physical directory path where generated image thumbnails are stored to speed up the UI.

cache.disk.location.long.text: The physical directory path where media previews and transcoded files are cached.

cache.thumbnail.size_limit_mb.long.text: The maximum amount of disk space in Megabytes the thumbnail cache is allowed to use. Oldest items are removed when this limit is reached.

cache.disk.size_limit_mb.long.text: The maximum amount of disk space in Megabytes the general disk cache can consume.

thumbnail.default.size.long.text: The standard dimension (in pixels) for generated thumbnails.

thumbnail.jpeg.quality.long.text: The compression quality level for generated thumbnails, ranging from 0 (lowest quality, smallest file) to 100 (highest quality, largest file).

thumbnail.qhd_preview.threshold_mb.long.text: Images larger than this file size will automatically have a lighter 'QHD' preview generated to improve loading times.

tpm.types.thumbnail_generator.share.long.text: The proportion of the thread pool allocated for generating image and video thumbnails.

media.filter.enabled.long.text: When enabled, media files that do not meet certain criteria (like minimum size) will be ignored.

media.filter.min_file_size_kb.long.text: Files smaller than this size in Kilobytes will be entirely ignored by the system.

media.filter.low_res.min_width.long.text: Images narrower than this width in pixels will be flagged as low resolution or ignored.

media.filter.low_res.min_height.long.text: Images shorter than this height in pixels will be flagged as low resolution or ignored.

media.filter.low_res.apply_after_date.lo.text: The date (in YYYY-MM-DD format) after which the low-resolution filters will be strictly applied. Older files may be exempt.

server.http.threadPool.maxThreads.long.text: The maximum number of threads dedicated to handling HTTP requests.

server.http.threadPool.maxQueued.long.text: The maximum number of HTTP requests that can be queued waiting for a thread before the server starts rejecting new requests.

database.sqlite.cacheSize.long.text: The number of pages SQLite keeps in memory to speed up database reads.

database.sqlite.tempStore.long.text: Determines where SQLite stores temporary tables and indices. Using 'memory' is faster but requires more RAM.

files.manager.useInMemoryIndex.long.text: Caches the file structure in RAM for much faster file lookups, at the cost of higher memory usage.

files.service.immediateJobTrigger.enable.text: Allows the file service to bypass the scheduler and instantly trigger scanning or processing when changes are detected.

files.service.immediateJobTrigger.timeou.text: The debounce or timeout duration before firing an immediate file change event, to group rapid changes together.

tpm.thread.stackSizeKB.long.text: The amount of memory allocated to each worker thread's stack. Adjust only if experiencing stack overflow issues.

tpm.mediaGeneration.maxConcurrent.long.text: Combined cap on thumbnail and preview generation tasks running at once. Each task launches an external ImageMagick decode that can use hundreds of MB for RAW files; unbounded bursts cause transient decode failures under memory pressure. Default 4.

tools.imagemagick.path.long.text: Full path to the ImageMagick 'magick' executable used for thumbnail and preview generation. Defaults to the Homebrew location /opt/homebrew/bin/magick.

media.processor.maxQueueSize.long.text: The maximum number of media items that can be queued up for processing simultaneously.

media.image.transcoding.enabled.long.text: Globally enables transcoding images from incompatible formats into standard formats before processing.

media.image.transcoding.timeoutMs.long.text: The maximum time allowed for transcoding a single image before giving up.

media.image.transcoding.preserveMetadata.text: Ensures that EXIF data, dates, and other metadata are copied from the original image to the transcoded image.

media.images.tif.long.text: Allows the system to read, index, and process files with the .tif extension.

duplicates.representative.strategy.long.text: The algorithmic strategy used to determine which file in a duplicate group should be considered the primary or 'best' file.

cache.thumbnail.clearOnStartup.long.text: Automatically empties the thumbnail directory every time the server starts. Useful for development or resolving cache corruption.

thumbnail.pipeline.enabled.long.text: Enables the new structured thumbnail processing pipeline for generating standard thumbnails.

thumbnail.pipeline.onlyIfMissing.long.text: When enabled, the pipeline skips thumbnail generation if an existing thumbnail of the correct size is already present.

media.adjustments.enabled.long.text: Crop and rotate edits made in the viewer. They never touch the source file: each edit is stored in a sidecar JSON next to the asset (or in the location's edits folder) and mirrored in the database. Off hides the tool panel and renders every image un-edited.

media.adjustments.sidecar.write.long.text: When off, edits are kept in the database only and no file is written beside the assets. They then do not travel with the library and are lost when the location is deregistered.

media.adjustments.preview.cacheBytes.lon.text: Bytes of intermediate frames each live-preview session keeps, so a slider on the last node re-renders one node instead of the whole chain. 384 MB holds about seven full-size frames at 2560 px.

media.adjustments.preview.sessions.long.text: How many files keep a decoded base image and node cache in memory for the viewer's live preview at once (the open file and its strip neighbours). The least recently used session is dropped first.

media.adjustments.preview.idleSeconds.lo.text: Seconds a live-preview session may sit unused before its memory is released.

media.adjustments.preview.sessionSide.lo.text: Longest side, in pixels, of the base image a live-preview session holds. Frames are rendered at this size at rest and at half of it while a control is being dragged.

media.adjustments.history.maxEntries.lon.text: Undo steps kept per photo, stored with its edits in the sidecar and the database. The oldest step is dropped when the limit is reached.

media.adjustments.recipes.builtin.long.text: Seed a few example recipes (a red-filter monochrome, a soft contrast, a warm vignette) when the recipe list is empty. They can be renamed or deleted like any other recipe.

media.adjustments.masks.enabled.long.text: Lane masks that find things in the picture: the subject, people, faces from the library, or whatever a text prompt describes. Each is computed once per photo on the original pixels and cached; editing never re-runs a detector. Off hides these mask sources; lanes that use them render unchanged.

media.adjustments.masks.size.long.text: Longest side, in pixels, of a cached detected mask. Larger masks follow edges more closely and take more disk; 1024 suits the detectors' own resolution.

media.adjustments.masks.promptModelPath..text: The CLIPSeg ONNX model that turns a text prompt ("the sky", "the red car") into a mask, and the fallback for the subject mask where Apple Vision is not available. Missing file: the Prompt source is hidden.

media.adjustments.masks.peopleModelPath..text: The person-segmentation ONNX model (MediaPipe selfie segmentation) behind the People mask. Missing file: the People source is hidden.

media.adjustments.masks.refineEncoderPat.text: The SlimSAM image encoder (ONNX). With both SAM files present, the Prompt, People and portable Subject masks are sharpened: every region the coarse model found is handed to SAM as a box plus interior points, and the sharp answer replaces it. Missing file: masks keep the coarse model's edge-aware upsample.

media.adjustments.masks.refineDecoderPat.text: The SlimSAM prompt encoder and mask decoder (ONNX), the second half of the sharpening model.

media.adjustments.masks.useCoreML.long.text: Run the mask models through the CoreML execution provider where available. Off runs them on the CPU, which is where the quantised models are fastest to start.

media.adjustments.export.defaultFormat.l.text: The format the export sheet proposes: jpeg (quality below), png (8-bit, lossless) or tiff (16-bit, LZW). An export renders the photo's chain at full resolution into a new file in the folder you pick; the original is never modified and the export is not added to the library unless the folder is inside a registered location.

media.adjustments.export.defaultQuality..text: JPEG quality (1-100) the export sheet proposes. 92 is visually lossless for photographs at a fraction of the size of 100.

media.adjustments.sidecar.suffix.long.text: Appended to the asset's full file name: DSC04624.JPG becomes DSC04624.JPG.vurio.json. Changing it does not rename existing sidecars; they are re-imported under the new name only if renamed by hand.

thumbnail.pipeline.size.long.text: The target dimension in pixels generated by the advanced thumbnail pipeline.

scheduler.jobs.long.text: A comma-separated list of manually defined static jobs to run on startup. Typically leave empty for automatic scheduling.

scheduler.maxConsecutiveFailures.long.text: The maximum number of times a scheduled task can fail in a row before the scheduler disables it or alerts.

media.face.enabled.long.text: Detect faces in your photos and group them into people on the PEOPLE tab. The sweep runs in the background and catches up on new photos automatically.

media.face.mergePurgeCutoff.long.text: How well a face must match its person group to stay in it. Faces below this bar are ringed amber in the group popup, and when groups are combined (or this value is changed) they are set aside for re-grouping — nothing is deleted, they simply return to the pool and are re-matched.

On this library, faces of different people score at most about 0.51 against each other, while the same person across photos scores 0.67 or higher. The default 0.53 sits just above the stranger band. Raising it purges more aggressively (may set aside hard angles and blurry shots); lowering it keeps more faces. 0 disables purging entirely.
